manual_derivations.derivation: Every degree-d monomial of S is uniquely z^alpha h^(d-|alpha|), |alpha|<=d. Its image is the distinct affine monomial z^alpha. This gives a basis bijection with R_<=d; hence delta_d is injective and surjective. Nonzero homogeneous polynomial image cannot vanish. The quotient and localized class can vanish, and neither statement decides presentation utility.

manual_derivations.quantity: Original-generator membership and two ideal inclusions
manual_derivations.derivation: Apply h=1 to h^k f=sum_i a_i F_i^h to obtain g=sum_i a_i(z,1)F_i. Thus each appended g lies in I. Retaining every F_i proves I subset (F,G_added) subset I. This proves equality of ideals, not merely root counts, and does not require radicality.

The slice degree before primitive normalization is D_h. Removing a common h^r replaces (f,k) by (f/h^r,k+r); total original certificate/search degree E remains unchanged. Primitive f has D_h=deg(delta(f)). Upper bounds become minima only after the complete candidate-specific lower systems are certified. W_d/solver/checker expansion degrees can exceed 8 and must remain in E_all_stages_max.

Stars-and-bars gives |S_E|=binomial(r+E,E) for r+1 homogeneous variables and |R_<=d|=binomial(r+d,d). For each nonzero original generator of degree d_i<=E, all degree E-d_i multipliers contribute binomial(r+E-d_i,E-d_i) raw rows. Zero and duplicate rows cannot shrink the declared universe or raw-row count.

J_A=x(x,y,h), so J_A:h=(x). Thus C_2,1=span{x^2,xy,xw,xh}, while J_A,2=span{x^2,xy,xh}; Q has one basis class [xw]. The witness h*xw=w*(F2^h-F1^h) is exact. Affinely x=F2-F1 lies in W_2 and then xw lies in W_2. The nonzero polynomial xw therefore has zero presentation utility at this slice. In S=K[x,y,w,h], M2 has 10 columns/3 raw rows and M3 has 20 columns/12 raw rows; J_A,3 has the nine distinct monomials x^3,x^2y,x^2w,x^2h,xy^2,xyw,xyh,xwh,xh^2.

J_B=xy(x,h), so J_B:h=(xy), J_B,2=0 and C_2,1=span{xy}. The exact witness is h*xy=F2^h-F1^h. Both original affine generators have degree 3, so W_2(F_B)=0. Q again has dimension 1 but xy is useful. M2 has 10 columns/0 raw rows and M3 has 20 columns/2 raw rows. These are source-aware monomial arguments valid over each field, not executed matrix ranks.

For F=(xy,xy+x), hx=F2^h-F1^h while W_1(F)=0. For k0/no-additional-generator mode, bypassing preprocessing and invoking exactly the same baseline on identical bytes makes the algebraic computation identical; timing identity is neither required nor inferred.

manual_derivations: For prime digit encoding, p>2^s and z_i in {0,1} make the integer-to-field map injective. The ambient polynomial equations remain over F_p with digit constraints; ordinary field arithmetic cannot be replaced by characteristic-two reduction.
The frozen odd S3 has terminal -4B(X+Y), and the binary S3 has squared pairwise-product sum plus XYZ+B. Both match the retrieved formulas under the declared curve hypotheses.

The universal 4x4 Sylvester determinant is a polynomial in the unspecialized coefficients, so later target/digit specialization preserves its polynomial value. Dropping specialized leading coefficients and rebuilding a lower-degree resultant changes that operation and can discard exceptional roots. No old S4 implementation is licensed by this audit.

For every actual signed decomposition, P1+P2 is either a finite K12 point, producing u in the finite chart, or O, producing x1=x2 and x3=x_R in the O chart. Conversely, all projected chart roots are filtered by every actual rational y lift, prime-subgroup membership and the exact group sum. Extra algebraic roots are permitted but cannot become accepted decompositions without those checks.

For an allowed nonidentity odd-prime-order point P, set R=P and a=x(P). Then u=x(2P) is finite; the two finite equations on core (a,a,a) are the same symmetric S3 equation, so that core has a finite-chart root. It also has an O-chart root. Projecting the finite root and enumerating all signs still returns (P,-P,P). Thus deletion of the O tag need not lose that recovered tuple. This is a source-aware symbolic branch argument, with no generated curve or point.

All digit equations split into distinct roots 0 and 1 over either solver field. Their quotient is a product of fields, so every further ordinary ideal containing them is radical on the complete cube. Synthetic ideals without those equations require their actual multiplicity-aware ideal certificates.
joint_reviews.group_formula_audit: Odd chord/tangent substitution yields x3=lambda^2-x1-x2 and inverse third-intersection ordinate. In the binary form, substituting y=lambda*x+nu gives third abscissa lambda^2+lambda+A+x1+x2 and inversion adds x3 to the ordinate. Tangency gives lambda=x+y/x for x!=0; x=0 doubles to O. All denominator-zero and identity cases are explicit. These are manual equations, not an implemented checker pass.
joint_reviews.root_completeness: Prime full domain 2^(m*s), Boolean finite 2^24 and O 2^12 are explicit. The independent original evaluator must verify full sets, chart tags and fibers; equal cardinalities alone are insufficient. Failed field/curve/base/null construction remains unavailable, with no substitute cell.
